method: BASELINE. Written straight from the deposited text with the writing-l4-rules skill (and references/regulative.md), from the seat of the individual to whom the law is applied, with the design defaults ruled on 2026-10-18 and the rulings on negatives of 2026-11-04 and 2026-11-05 (JUST FALSE where the text says no, NOTHING where it does not answer); the date arithmetic (O. 3, O. 68 r. 5, Easter computed) in one module, the rules in another, the questions in a seat module importing them; three regulative rules (O. 20 r. 1, O. 24A rr. 3(4), 4) run by EVALTRACE inside exported questions that take only plain dates; no REFUSE; checked with the stable l4 of VS Code extension 1.6.98, JL4_LIBRARY_PATH unset. No pipeline, no coverage table, no independent test pass, no human gate.
edition_encoded: Rules of the Supreme Court 1971 (WA), consolidated version 09-am0-00 (currency from 11 December 2025), as deposited at ../../registers/source-bundle/mrdoc_49048.txt, retrieved 2026-11-06. Amendments after retrieval are not in the text.

seat: the plaintiff: a person bringing a claim (for example for damages for personal injury) in the Supreme Court of Western Australia by writ, including a child or other person under disability suing by a next friend (rsc-seat.l4)

checks.l4: stable l4 of VS Code extension legalese.l4-vscode 1.6.98, JL4_LIBRARY_PATH unset
checks.command: l4 run rsc-dates.l4 ; l4 run rsc-rules.l4 ; l4 run rsc-seat.l4 ; l4 run rsc-cases.l4
checks.result: 190 assertions written, 190 satisfied, 3 #TRACE FULFILLED, 0 errors, 0 warnings in every file (2026-11-07)
checks.note: l4 run exits 0 even when an assertion fails, so the diagnostics are what was read. Expected values worked by hand from the text and a calendar.

scope: The Orders a plaintiff meets from writ to judgment or settlement. In: O. 3 rr. 1-4, 7; O. 4A rr. 24, 28; O. 5 r. 11; O. 7 rr. 1(1), (2), 4; O. 9 r. 1(2), (4); O. 13 rr. 1-9; O. 14 r. 1(1); O. 20 rr. 1, 4, 5(4), 20(1); O. 23 rr. 2, 4; O. 24A rr. 3, 4, 5(1), 8, 9, 10(3)-(7A); O. 25 rr. 1, 2, 6; O. 28 r. 1(1), (2), (2A), (4), (5); O. 68 r. 5; O. 70 rr. 1, 2(1), (4), 10, 11, 12(1). Out: the rest (case management machinery, forms and service of documents, the defendant's side, discovery, trial, evidence, enforcement, other remedies, appeals, costs scales, office machinery, probate, family provision procedure, other Acts' rules). Reasons in NOTES.md.
